svg.aria-label: one_training_step and surprise_score, line by line, with handwritten notes. Step 1, pick_snippets: 32 snippets of 128 letters from random places in the practice text. Step 2, surprise_score for each snippet: the black box guesses every letter, and its surprise is scored. The 32 surprise scores are averaged into one number for the whole step, over 32 times 128 practice questions. The last step's slopes are cleared, because PyTorch would add the new ones on top. Step 3, backward: work backwards to a slope for every one of the 826,433 numbers. Step 4, nudge_every_number: AdamW moves every number a tiny way against its slope. Inside surprise_score: the black box gives 65 scores after every letter; softmax turns each row into 65 chances that add up to 1; positions numbers the rows; the chances of the letters that really came next are picked out; minus the log of each is its surprise, 0 if it was sure and right and 4.17 for a blind 1 in 65 guess; and the snippet's surprise score is the average of its 128 surprises.
